categories.contrast: Mixed: own praise and opponent criticism

ad_strategy.definition: Shares of all exact party/messages, not just messages describing people. Own-side praise is an endorsed positive description of a supported person or collective with the advertiser's party; opponent criticism is an endorsed negative description of an opposing-party person or collective. Mixed/contrast requires both in the same message. 'Only' means one of these two signals without the other; other sentiments can coexist. Neither is not neutral. Same-party rivals, unknown target parties, quoted opponents and rebutted or unclear voices do not supply these signals. Uncertain, unreviewed and stale messages stay in the denominator but are reported separately, never classified as neither. Displayed percentages are rounded.

denominator: Exact party/messages deduplicated after filters. Tone/frame shares use reviewed messages with an endorsed, in-scope description. No description is not neutral. Negative-only / positive-only / mixed / neutral-only are mutually exclusive. Mixed means positive and negative descriptions in that scope, possibly of different people. Inclusive negative and positive overlap through mixed messages; frames also overlap.

method: AI-assisted full-text semantic review of each exact party/message, not keyword proximity or a sentiment lexicon. Descriptions must concern a person or political collective and retain an exact claim passage and target anchor. Labels describe the advertiser's portrayal, not whether its claim is true. These labels are not independently validated human gold.

categories.contrast: Mixed: own praise and opponent criticism

ad_strategy.definition: Shares of all exact party/messages, not just messages describing people. Own-side praise is an endorsed positive description of a supported person or collective with the advertiser's party; opponent criticism is an endorsed negative description of an opposing-party person or collective. Mixed/contrast requires both in the same message. 'Only' means one of these two signals without the other; other sentiments can coexist. Neither is not neutral. Same-party rivals, unknown target parties, quoted opponents and rebutted or unclear voices do not supply these signals. Uncertain, unreviewed and stale messages stay in the denominator but are reported separately, never classified as neither. Displayed percentages are rounded.
